title: Deployment decision canvas and traffic scenarios (working notes)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight decision canvas + execution notes for cross-functional rollouts that combine canary deployments and A/B experiments. The goal is to give PM/Eng/SRE/QA/Support a single-page set of heuristics and traffic scenarios so that teams can choose a rollout pattern quickly and consistently.

Intended audience: product managers running feature launches in the Console, platform engineers configuring routing policies, SRE on-call, and solutions engineers supporting customers.

High-level decision questions (use top-down):
- Is the change user-visible (affects outputs/UX) or infra-only (performance/cost)?
- Is the feature reversible via config/flag or does it require code changes to revert?
- Does the rollout touch stateful subsystems or customer data paths (KV cache, billing hooks)?
- What is the blast radius tolerance (single user, 1% of traffic, region-wide)?
- Is there a safety fallback (alternative model variant, region fallback, degrade to cached responses)?
- What SLOs are most at risk (p50 latency, p99 latency, error rate, quality regressions)?

Decision canvas (quick mapping to a pattern):
- Infra-only + reversible + low-blast -> Progressive rollout with quick scaling test (no A/B).
- User-visible + reversible + low-blast -> Canary (1% -> 5% -> 20%) with baseline metric comparison and manual gates.
- User-visible + non-reversible or requires data migration -> Internal dogfood -> Beta cohort -> Full launch.
- High risk quality/regression concerns -> A/B experiment with gated analysis, cohort split, and automated hold back.

Traffic scenarios (matrix) - pick row that matches your change:
- Scenario A: Small feature flag toggle (cosmetic)
  - Start: 2% of random traffic for 24h
  - Ramp: 2% -> 10% (48h) -> 25% (72h) -> 100% (if stable)
  - Guardrails: no increase in error rate by >0.5pp, no >10% regression on task success metrics
  - Rollback: immediate if errors spike or customer complaints > threshold

- Scenario B: Model variant swap for hosted API (quality/cost tradeoff)
  - Start: 0.5% to internal + 0.5% to invited customers for 48h
  - Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 15% with continuous A/B quality checks on embeddings/certainty metrics
  - Metrics: embedding cosine similarity distribution, downstream task regressions, p50/p95 latency
  - Fallback: automatic routing to previous variant when p99 latency > baseline * 1.5 or quality regression > 3%

- Scenario C: Large infra change (runtime kernel upgrade)
  - Start: Canary on dedicated capacity pool (pre-sliced) with synthetic load + small production slice (0.1%)
  - Ramp: expand synthetic load coverage, then 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% controlled by Autoscale policy
  - Observability: trace sampling bumped to 100% for canary slices for 24h
  - Rollback: automated drain and routing away from upgraded nodes if tail latency or OOMs occur

Canary scheduling heuristics (practical rules):
- Minimum observation window: at least 48 hours or 5M tokens processed, whichever is longer.
- For noise-prone metrics (user satisfaction), prefer at least 7 days to capture weekday/weekend patterns.
- Use progressive doubling for early ramps (0.5% -> 1% -> 2% -> 4%) then bigger jumps (10% -> 25% -> 50%).
- Always include an internal-only cohort (employees + test customers) before public slices.

Metrics and guardrails (tiered):
- Primary safety metrics (must check every step): error rate (4xx/5xx), p99 latency, request timeouts, model OOMs, infra CPU/GPU saturation.
- Primary quality metrics (user-visible): task success rate, precision/recall proxies, embedding-drifts, manual score samples.
- Secondary business metrics: revenue-impacting signals, retention, usage volume.
- Statistical thresholds: prefer absolute delta thresholds for safety (e.g., p99 latency +1s) and relative % for quality (e.g., >2% regression triggers hold).
- Alerting: automatic paged alert if safety metrics breach AND sustained for >5 minutes; for quality regressions page on sustained >60 minutes plus sample review.

Observability plan (what to enable during canary/experiment):
- Increase traces for canary slices and highlight traces that include model-fallbacks.
- Turn on token-level cost breakdown for canary traffic to catch unexpected cost regressions.
- Capture and store representative sample of responses (redacted) for manual QA and bias checks.
- Activate console-level experiment dashboard: metric diffs, time-series, heatmap of customer impact.

Experiment config template (copy-paste for Console):
- experiment_name: short-slug
- hypothesis: one-sentence hypothesis + expected magnitude
- cohorts: internal, invited-beta, random-public
- slices: percentage per cohort and ramp schedule with timestamps
- success_criteria: list of metrics + thresholds + evaluation window
- safety_cutoffs: list of metrics + immediate action (pause/rollback/auto-fallback)
- observability_flags: trace_sampling=100, sample_responses=1000/day
- ticket_links: jira id, runbook link

Rollback and remediation playbook (short):
1) Pause ramping immediately (Console toggle).
2) If safety metric breached -> auto-switch routing to baseline variant and escalate to SRE.
3) If quality regression -> pause, snapshot logs and a sample of user responses, create hotfix PR if root cause identified.
4) Communication: notify stakeholders on Slack channel + postmortem channel.

Comms and coordination checklist (who does what):
- PM: owns hypothesis, success criteria, customer comms plan.
- Dev lead: config and rollout steps in Console, PR link, rollback procedure written.
- SRE: monitors infra signals, ready to execute node-level rollback.
- QA: runs manual sample reviews at each ramp and signs off before next step.
- Support: briefed with canned responses and escalation path.
- Solutions Eng: monitors invited customers and coordinates feedback.

Post-launch and experiment analysis notes:
- Always compute both relative and absolute deltas. Small relative deltas on low-volume metrics can be noisy.
- Use stratified slicing (by region, client tier, model version) to catch heterogeneous effects.
- Save a sample of pre-change and post-change responses for offline human review for at least 30 days.
- Run a short A/B quality audit: blind evaluation of 200 samples from each cohort.

Short template for a one-paragraph release note to customers: "We rolled out an experimental model variant to a small percentage of traffic to test performance and accuracy improvements. If you experience increased latency or unexpected outputs, please contact support and include the request id. We will roll back if any regression is detected."

Open questions / notes-to-self (needs alignment with Console engineering):
- Can the Console support time-of-day scheduled ramps (e.g., only ramp during 10:00-18:00 PST)? If not, we must add to feature backlog.
- Need a lightweight way to mark an experiment as customer-impacting in Dashboard so CS gets alerted earlier.
- How do we ledger cost anomalies per experiment automatically? Token-level cost tagging currently manual.
- Evaluate adding a Canary CDF-based test for latency tail shifts rather than point p99 checks.

Quick action items (next 2 sprints):
- Add experiment config template to Console UI (PM + Eng).
- Implement auto-tagging of telemetry by experiment id (Infra).
- Draft Support canned responses and embed in runbook templates (Ops + Support).
- Run a dry-run internal kickoff for the next dedicated deployment (simulate 0.5% -> 2% ramp).

Appendix: shorthand checklists
- Pre-launch: hypothesis written, success criteria, fallbacks listed, internal cohort tested, runbook created, stakeholders notified.
- During: observe safety metrics, sample outputs, get QA sign-off for each ramp, check cost signals.
- Post: A/B analysis, blind human review, update docs, postmortem if unexpected regression.

End of working notes.

(Notes: this doc intentionally concise—expanding into a full playbook is next step. Keep this as the rapid-decision canvas that teams can copy and adapt.)
